text:
aya: noticed a customer on the support ticket complaining about p95 spiking to ~700ms for inference in us-central this morning. they say it started ~08:10 UTC and persists. filing here to correlate with infra changes.

matt: ACK. any correlated deploys or infra changes around that time?

eli: support forwarded traceroute and some curl timings from the customer's side. posting the curl from their host (public ip redacted):\n\n```\n$ time curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{time_starttransfer}\n' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\n0.68\nreal 0m0.69s\n```\n\nThey also reported TLS handshake durations symptomatic of an extra RTT.

jun: looking at edge metrics now. I see spike in TLS handshake latency for us-central POPs at 08:08-08:18 UTC, p95 jumped from ~60ms to ~480ms. p99 up to 1.2s. No deploys in control plane at that exact time per deploy-bot.

sre-oncall: deploy-bot confirms no code deploys, but a config push to the NLB routing weights happened at 08:05 (automated traffic rebalancer) — not a full service deploy. Could that have steered traffic into a path with cross-zone hairpin?

jun: I pulled the route affinity metrics. At 08:04 we had an influx of connections being routed to a new egress NAT pair in us-central-2 which sits in a different AZ than the frontend POP. That could add an extra AZ hop and increase handshake RTT.

aya: customer says they started seeing the latency right after an internal maintenance window, but that was in their infra. they were routed through our API endpoint the whole time.

matt: can we correlate client IP -> edge POP -> egress path? add a few sample traces from our side (ingress logs).

jun: pasted three sample ingress events (anonymized):\n\n```\ningress: 2026-02-28T08:06:12Z client_ip=X.X.X.X pop=us-central-1 egress_nic=eni-12345 az=us-central-1a route_affinity=stale\ningress: 2026-02-28T08:07:03Z client_ip=Y.Y.Y.Y pop=us-central-1 egress_nic=eni-67890 az=us-central-1b route_affinity=stale\ningress: 2026-02-28T08:09:30Z client_ip=Z.Z.Z.Z pop=us-central-2 egress_nic=eni-54321 az=us-central-2a route_affinity=sticky\n```\nNote the mix of pops and AZs. We had some hairpinning between us-central-1 and us-central-2 during the window.

eli: customer traceroute (their path):\n\n```\ntraceroute to api.redwood.example (34.120.10.7), 30 hops max\n 1  10.0.0.1  0.23 ms\n 2  100.65.10.1  12.02 ms\n 3  gn-1.example.net  15.45 ms\n 4  us-central-1-edge  18.12 ms\n 5  us-central-2-egress  110.34 ms\n 6  34.120.10.7  110.88 ms\n```\nShows a jump when crossing to us-central-2 egress.

matt: ok looks like route rebalancer changed weights at 08:05 and that caused some traffic to be routed via us-central-2 egress which is across AZs. That explains the extra RTT and handshake inflation.

sre-oncall: recommended mitigations: 1) revert the rebalancer weight to previous baseline, 2) lower DNS TTL for affected edge dns entries temporarily, 3) add per-POP sticky routing for 30m to stabilize.

jun: I can revert weight now. doing a dry-run and then commit.\n\n```\n# dry-run\n$ rebalancer simulate --region us-central --from-weight 0.25 --to-weight 0.05\nok: predicted shift of 6% of traffic out of us-central-2\n```\ncommit in 30s.

deploy-bot: rebalancer commit scheduled by jun at 2026-02-28T08:18:01Z

jun: commit done at 08:18:01Z. monitoring.

aya: notifying customer that we performed a rollback of routing weights and are monitoring. asked for a new curl/traceroute after 2m.

eli: customer responded with new curl at 08:21:30Z: `0.072` time_starttransfer. they say latency back to normal for them.

eli: customer happy, but asks for RCA and prevention steps.

matt: root cause: automated traffic rebalancer over-corrected and introduced cross-AZ egress when affinity/sticky sessions were still warming. This produced extra network hops and inflated TLS handshake RTTs, driving p95/p99 regression for affected POP.

jun: follow-ups I propose:
- make rebalancer respect active affinity (don't move traffic that has sticky session > 1m)
- add safety cap: never move more than X% traffic per minute across AZs
- add telemetry alert when handshake latency delta between p50 and p95 exceeds 200ms and correlate with route changes
- add automated rollback trigger if p95 increases >300ms within 10m of a rebalancer action

sre-oncall: also recommend we pre-provision egress NATs in each POP (reduce cross-AZ egress) and make canonical egress mapping explicit in the control plane.

aya: billing angle: customer asked if they were billed for the slow requests — they were, but we should offer a credit. I'll coordinate with SRE and Support to propose a goodwill credit for the spike window.

eli: I filed customer follow-up and will deliver a summary once we have postmortem notes.

matt: I'll own the postmortem. tagging Jun and Aya for mitigation tasks. please create tickets for rebalancer changes and egress mapping.

jun: created tickets: REBAL-402 (safety caps), REBAL-403 (affinity-aware moves), EGRESS-88 (pre-provision egress per POP). links: https://tracker/REBAL-402

sre-oncall: closing the thread once tickets are in motion and customer confirmed. thanks team :thumbsup:

aya: thanks all — customer confirmed restored perf and appreciated the quick roll-back.

deploy-bot: no active deploys in the last 30m.
